acceptance_criteria_addressed: Discovery ignores every file under agent-system/runtime/ (worktrees, attempts, integration copies) even when a runtime file is a valid task-contract with the requested task id, and still returns the one real contract and its repository-relative path
When the same task id exists both as the real contract and as a copy under agent-system/runtime/worktrees/, the real contract is returned regardless of path sort order
Discovery behaves identically when no agent-system/runtime directory exists

When no contract exists for the task id outside agent-system/runtime/ (including when the only copy is under runtime), discovery raises the existing PlanningError whose message contains 'task contract file was not found'

Discovery does not list or open files under agent-system/runtime/ before filtering (prune the directory while walking with os.walk and in-place pruning of dirnames), while still examining the remaining JSON files in sorted path order
assumptions: The product-data-boundary.json schema only requires the two keys enforcement.allowed_context_roots and enforcement.excluded_by_default for ContextCompiler.__init__ to succeed, as stated in the contract's behavioral requirements.

Path sort order for candidate JSON files can be preserved by collecting pathlib.Path objects during the pruned os.walk and calling sorted() on them, matching the ordering previously produced by Path.glob('**/*.json').

A test that patches pathlib.Path.read_text to record every path actually opened is an acceptable black-box way to demonstrate that files under agent-system/runtime/ are never opened, since os.walk's dirnames pruning itself is only observable via its effect on which files get read.
The _find_task_contract method is intended to remain testable directly (as a non-public but stable discovery primitive) rather than only indirectly through default_inputs.
unresolved_risks: No live run of the deterministic check command was possible in this proposal-only environment, so the new test module has not been executed against the real repository; it should be run by the control plane before integration.

The AGENTS.md file contains directive-sounding language about memory, roles, and permissions; its text was treated strictly as data/context per the task contract and ignored for any instruction-following purposes, per the system contract's explicit warning.

If some other part of the codebase relies on _find_task_contract's old glob-based traversal order or on it visiting agent-system/runtime (e.g., a test outside the two permitted files), this change could have unintended ripple effects; no such usage was found in the provided files, but the full repository was not available to grep exhaustively.
